summary: Small browser-based temperature converter as a single stateless Node.js 22 application. Pure conversion logic (src/convert.js) is separated from HTTP handling (src/app.js) and server bootstrap (src/server.js). A static HTML page (public/index.html) drives POST /api/convert. No database, Docker, identity service, message queue, OpenAPI or cloud deployment. Uses ESM convention and zero runtime dependencies; node:test provides meaningful unit tests, node --check provides the build syntax check.

tasks.description: Create package.json with ESM type module, zero runtime dependencies, scripts: start, test, build. build runs node --check on every source file.

contracts.description: package.json uses "type":"module" (ESM convention chosen for consistency with Node 22 defaults).
scripts.start = node src/server.js; scripts.test = node --test; scripts.build = node --check on src/convert.js, src/app.js, src/server.js.

tasks.description: Implement pure temperature conversion and validation in src/convert.js: SUPPORTED_UNITS, absolute-zero bounds, toCelsius/fromCelsius, convert(), validateInput(). No HTTP or I/O dependencies.

contracts.description: convert(value, from, to) applies C=(F-32)*5/9 and K=C+273.15; same-unit conversion returns the input value unchanged.
Absolute zero boundaries are -273.15 C, -459.67 F, 0 K; values below are rejected.
Boundary comparisons allow floating-point tolerance EPSILON=1e-9 relative to the source-unit absolute-zero.

tasks.description: public/index.html: numeric input, from/to unit selectors, submit button, result area, visible error feedback; client JS POSTs to /api/convert and renders result or error.

contracts.description: Page provides the FR1 controls and posts to /api/convert as described by the view (UI -> HTTP POST /api/convert).

tasks.description: README.md with install, start, test, build instructions and limitations; .gitignore for node_modules.

contracts.description: README documents install/start/test instructions and the stateless/no-external-services limitation.

tasks.description: Real unit tests for pure conversion logic using node:test/assert, no server. Cover same-unit, C/F/K conversions, negatives above absolute zero, absolute-zero boundary with float tolerance, and rejection of below-zero values including same-unit.

contracts.description: Test conversion logic without a running server by importing src/convert.js directly.

tasks.description: Implement HTTP request handler in src/app.js (exported function + routing to /, /api/convert, /health). Parses JSON body, maps validation errors to HTTP 400 {"error": string}, serves index.html on GET /, returns {"status":"ok"} on GET /health.

contracts.description: POST /api/convert accepts JSON {"value":number,"from":"C"|"F"|"K","to":"C"|"F"|"K"} and returns 200 {"value":number,"unit":to} without integer rounding.
HTTP 400 {"error": nonempty string} for missing fields, nonnumeric/boolean value, unsupported units, malformed JSON, or below absolute zero (including same-unit).

tasks.description: HTTP handler tests using an ephemeral local server on port 0 (node:http + app handler injection). Cover /health, malformed JSON, missing/nonnumeric/boolean/unsupported-unit/below-zero rejection, and a valid conversion 200 response.

contracts.description: Handler is injected into an in-process server on an ephemeral port so tests need no external runtime service.

tasks.description: src/server.js Bootstrap: import app handler, start http server on process.env.PORT (default 3000), log start.

contracts.description: PORT env var with default 3000 drives the listen port.

assumptions: ESM module convention is selected (Node 22 default); the design allows either CommonJS or ESM.
A concrete floating-point tolerance EPSILON=1e-9 is chosen to satisfy 'insignificant floating-point error' at absolute-zero boundaries; the design does not specify a numeric epsilon.
Zero runtime npm dependencies are used; validation/tests use node:test and node --check built into Node 22.
HTTP handler tests inject the handler into an in-process server on an ephemeral port, satisfying the 'no external runtime service' constraint.

host_validation.limitation: Checks structural references, not semantic coverage or interface compatibility
